Manufacturing Assembly Operator-Lafayette, GA

USA, LaFayette, GA

Role Summary

The Assembly Operator role contributes to manufacturing operations by assembling appliance components and subassemblies in alignment with standard work, quality expectations, and safety requirements. The role requires consistent execution of tasks, collaboration within a team environment, and the ability to meet production demands.

Core Responsibilities

• Assemble components and subassemblies according to documented standard work

• Operate basic manufacturing equipment and hand tools safely and effectively

• Perform repetitive production tasks while maintaining quality and productivity standards

• Conduct basic visual inspections to ensure product conformance

• Escalate safety, quality, or equipment concerns to appropriate personnel

• Maintain an organized and safe workstation

• Support team objectives and production goals

Minimum Requirements

• Legally authorized to work in the United States

• Minimum of one (1) year of work experience

• 18 years of age or older (17 if a work-based learning high school student)

• Ability to meet background, drug screening, and physical requirements

• Ability to perform essential job functions with or without reasonable accommodation.

Required Competencies

Safety & Compliance

• Demonstrates consistent adherence to safety policies, procedures, and PPE requirements

• Identifies and reports potential hazards or unsafe conditions

Quality Focus

• Follows standard work and quality requirements accurately

• Performs self-checks and visual inspections to ensure product quality

• Understands the impact of individual work on overall product performance

Execution & Reliability

• Completes assigned tasks consistently and on time

• Maintains focus and efficiency in a repetitive work environment

• Demonstrates dependability and accountability for assigned work

Teamwork & Communication

• Collaborates effectively with team members, leads, and supervisors

• Communicates issues clearly and respectfully

• Contributes to a positive and collaborative work environment

Continuous Improvement Mindset

• Demonstrates openness to learning and feedback

• Supports process improvements and standard work updates

• Identifies opportunities to improve safety, quality, or efficiency

Physical & Job Demands

Material Handling

• Lifting: negligible weight and up to 10 lbs. constantly; up to 20 lbs. frequently; up to 25 lbs. occasionally; no lifting greater than 25 lbs.

• Carrying: negligible weight and up to 10 lbs. constantly; up to 20 lbs. fre quently; up to 25 lbs. occasionally; no carrying greater than 25 lbs.

• Pushing/Pulling: negligible force constantly; up to 10 lbs. force frequently; up to 20 lbs. and up to 25 lbs. force occasionally; no pushing or pulling forces exceeding 40 lbs.

Positional Tolerances

• Sitting: 0.0 hours per workday

• Standing: up to 7.0 hours per workday

• Walking: up to 1.0 hour per workday

• Foot/leg controls: up to 1.0 hour per workday

Postural Activities

• Occasional (up to 1/3 of the time): kneeling, squatting, crawling, and climbing

• Frequent (up to 2/3 of the time): bending and turning/twisting

• Constant (more than 2/3 of the time): reaching outward up to 20 inches; reaching overhead up to 60 inches; wrist turning; grasping; pinching; and fine finger manipulation

Equipment Use

• Vibrating tools: constant use tolerated

Environmental Conditions

• Temperature and humidity levels consistent with current outdoor conditions

• Bright manufacturing lighting

• Hearing protection is required in designated areas of the Fab/Fin manufacturing footprint

The Senior Advanced Manufacturing Engineer (AME) for Plastics is knowledgeable in injection mold tooling and processing, molding equipment, and plastics part design. This role involves managing tooling and equipment projects by executing necessary activities at each milestone throughout the project. The Senior AME plays a pivotal role in guiding and mentoring entry level AMEs within the team on how to manage and execute projects.

This role also serves as a lead technical/engineering liaison for the Center of Excellence (COE), which is the internal plastics “supplier” of all Appliance Park in-house molded products.

Position
Senior Advanced Manufacturing Engineer – Plastics

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

How You'll Create Possibilities

Manufacturing Project Management:

· Provides technical COE guidance for all processes, cross-functional team meetings, and design reviews for injection molds, injection molding presses and associated automation equipment

· Support the GE Appliances Business Change Request (BCR) process

· Take a lead role managing multiple simultaneous projects

· Develop technical specifications to ensure accurate and timely delivery of associated molds/equipment

· Ensure Equipment Qualification projects are accurately created in Oracle Agile as the primary AME project management process

· Drive projects through each milestone completion with necessary stakeholder engagement and ensure Agile is updated in a timely manner

· Ability to manage and report on capital spending, project timeline/delivery status and other KPI related aspects of a project

Safety, Quality, Productivity, Cost:

· Maintain certified Lock Out (LOTO) status for safe equipment operation

· Lead supplier Risk Assessment review and EHS approvals of all applicable equipment

· Provide guidance on part dimensional and tolerance requirements to ensure Design for Manufacturability (DFM)

· Join Cross-functional teams to resolve part design or equipment requirement issues

· Collaborate with Plastics CAE experts to analyze design, quality and productivity related aspects of new plastic part designs

· Lead RFQ process for quotes, summarize and recommend suppliers to achieve low cost, on time results

· Track supplier delivery and provide accountability to avoid timeline delays

· Provide communication within the COE team to ensure smooth plant implementation of molds and equipment

What You'll Bring to Our Team

Minimum Requirements:

· Ability to collaborate effectively across multiple levels of the organization to promote operational success and continuous improvement

· High energy, initiative, and motivation to contribute to a team-oriented environment

· Organizational skills with the ability to manage simultaneous projects and tasks efficiently

· Strong problem-solving abilities and follow-through on initiatives

Minimum Qualifications:

· 5+ years of experience in injection molding or manufacturing engineering

· Experience with injection molding equipment, resin delivery systems, robotic part load/unload systems, and injection mold troubleshooting

· Equipment procurement experience (quoting, sourcing, implementation)

· Project Management experience in a cross-functional manufacturing environment

Preferred Qualifications:

· Bachelor of Science in Engineering degree (plastics / mechanical / manufacturing engineering / industrial / electrical)

· Hands-on experience in injection molding part/mold design, molding machines and/or automated equipment operations

· Moldflow/Moldex CAE working knowledge

· CAD experience

· RJG injection molding knowledge

· Sepro and/or Fanuc Robotics experience

Working Conditions:

· Working conditions are normal for both an office and manufacturing environments.

· Work may involve lifting materials and products up to 25 pounds.

· Working in the manufacturing environment requires the use of safety equipment to include but not limited to safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves, work shoes/boots.

· Work will include walking and standing for extended periods, using stairs, cross-overs and ladders.

The AME Finishes COE Engineer is responsible for leading and executing projects in support of the Global Finishes COE Strategy. This involves extensive cross-functional team engagement and individual leadership. The AME Finishes COE Engineer will be responsible for CapEx projects related to internal coating operations as well as supporting improvement projects with external coating operations. The candidate will support the Finishes COE Hoshin goals and deliver improved operations performance for Premium Finishes. This role will interact heavily with Factory Operations, Technology, Supplier Quality, Sourcing, and Advanced Manufacturing. In addition, this role will develop and implement improved processes and control methods for internal factories as well as external suppliers.

Position
Advanced Manufacturing Engineer – Finishes COE

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

How You'll Create Possibilities

• Participate in growing the Finishes COE organization’s overall capability and business impact.  This includes adding to the body of knowledge of the COE, individual training, and understanding of new manufacturing processes.

• Support the Finishes COE Hoshin to include the global strategy for Premium Finishes management, architecture and standards, processes, and appearance control.

• Support large investment CapEx projects related to internal finishing operations.  This would include optimization of current systems, upgrading existing equipment, investigation of new technologies, and integration of equipment into the factories.

• Create equipment specifications for Finishing CapEx projects to procure the correct advanced technology and ensure system compatibility.

• Provide analysis of incumbent coating methods and controls and ensure they conform to GEA standards, processes, and initiatives.

• Own all aspects of advanced manufacturing engineering and project management for internal and external assigned coating operations.  This includes the qualification of new materials, as well as continuous ownership and development throughout the life cycle of the finishing operation.

• Utilize technical expertise in finishes and manufacturing equipment to improve factory processes and overall operational performance.

• Lead finishes improvement projects in a matrix environment by partnering with Technology, EHS, AME, and Manufacturing teams.

• Interface with coating suppliers, applicators, and manufacturing sites to improve coatings initiatives for the business.

• Identify new coating’s processes, tools, and contacts within the industry – including new suppliers, instruments, or processes to further advance the business.

• Utilize the Finishes Execution Scorecard, Technical Audits, and other quality tools to identify and drive quality projects across all coatings operations resulting in the overall improvement of Premium Finishes at GEA.

• Monitor and resolve coatings process control performance issues by adhering to quality control plans and implementing sustainable corrective actions

• Drive permanent resolution of coatings and finishes Cost of Quality issues caused by manufacturing and supplier defects.

• Lead projects involving coatings supplier moves, process and material changes.  Support design change projects.

• Support the GEA finishes commercial strategy through qualification of alternate suppliers and materials, data collection of current process state, and integration with the operations and equipment requirements.

• Lead problem definition and reactive problem solving of coatings issues through disciplined root cause and corrective action.

• Provide clear and concise project status updates to leadership teams.

• Identify areas for cost reduction within coatings and finishing processes both internal and external.

What You'll Bring to Our Team

Requirements and Qualifications:

• Engineering or Technical degree (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics) or equivalent technical experience

• Minimum 2 years Advanced Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, and/or Technical experience in manufacturing environment

• Minimum 2 years of CapEx project leadership in coating/finishes.

• Understanding of statistical tools for process and product development and control (i.e. Gage R&R, Process Capability, Control Plans, SPC, Process Failure Mode Effects Analysis (PFMEA) and Design of Experiments (DOEs)).

• Understanding of with problem solving tools and component qualification (i.e., 8-D, 5 Whys, 7 Ways, DOE, eCAR, Fishbone, Pareto, Six Sigma, First Piece, PPAP).

• Experience with coatings, physical evaluation methods and measurement techniques.

• Basic understanding of color and appearance control methods.

• Project management and organizational skills

• Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally

• Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written

• Ability to influence and drive change within a highly matrixed organization.

Desired Qualifications:

• Prior NPI program experience

• Six Sigma Certification

• Proficient in MS Office, MS Scheduler (or equivalent) and AutoCAD

Our Control Technicians support appliance manufacturing operations to provide continuously monitor process parameters required to produce the highest quality part and product with the least scrap. Maintain process controls, robot programs and other systems, including injection molding and vacuum forming in support of safety, quality, delivery, and meeting cost objectives for our Decatur operations.

Position
Control Technician II - Support Operations

Location
USA, Decatur, AL

How You'll Create Possibilities

Under the direction of the area leader (supervisor) or manager, the process control technician will be responsible for processing, setup and troubleshooting of the machines and equipment in their assigned work area. They are responsible for ensuring adherence to safety, quality, housekeeping, and company policies, procedures and standards.

Essential Job Responsibilities:

• Responsible for troubleshooting, setup, loading, transferring, operating and adjusting processes, and the associated production equipment.

• Perform routine and preventive maintenance and troubleshoot equipment malfunctions.

• Complete changeovers as needed; changing dies; and performing manual tool changeovers converting the fixtures to run and trial different size configurations as needed.

• Work with operations leadership to prioritize work and meet critical deadlines.

• Work with quality, engineering, maintenance, etc. to help prepare for trials, assist in operations, and handle the disposition of test or scrap materials.

• Proactively lead the troubleshooting & analyzing of assigned equipment / machines and processes. Implement actions and help document and track processes for improvement.

• Use technology including PLC’s, smart boards, tv screens, kiosks on the shop floor to monitor equipment.

• Ability to rotate among jobs within the department and know all aspects of the production process.

• Maintain a clean work environment and follow all company policies and practices regarding safety and material handling.

• Utilize a forklift to maneuver parts, materials and dies in the area.

• All other duties as assigned.

• Why GE Appliances?

• Medical, dental and vision benefits starting day one

• Tuition reimbursement and career development

• Generous 401k plan with company contributions

• Paid vacation, holiday, and personal time

• Paid parental leave

• On-site cafeteria and credit union

• And, so much more!

What You'll Bring to Our Team

Minimum Requirements:

• High school diploma, GED or equivalent; associate’s degree in a technical field preferred.

• One or more years of experience in a job involving manufacturing   machine setup, troubleshooting and mold change, preferably in a high-volume environment.

• Requires knowledge of PLC and must be capable of making minor adjustments.

• Experience working with injection molding and/or vacuum forming processes preferred.

• Must have attention to detail and have ability to work with tight tolerances (+/- .0005 - .002).

• Must be able to work independently.

• Must be capable of working around moving machines, robots, equipment, forklifts, etc.

• Requires mechanical aptitude and ability to understand basic mechanical concepts and relationships.

• Available to work weekends and extended hours as needed, as well as shutdowns.

• You must be legally authorized to work in the United States without restriction.

• You must be able to follow verbal and written instructions in English.

• Must pass a background check and drug screen.

• Must be able to successfully complete physical confirming satisfactory health for job and have the ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without an accommodation, including, but not limited to:

•  Occasionally lift up to 50 lbs., with potential heavy lifting up to 75 lbs.

• Must be able to access required areas pertaining to job including, but not limited to: foam rooms, chemicals, high noise, and other areas of the plant.

• Job may require the use of a respirator at times; therefore, candidates must complete an annual medical evaluation to safely wear a respirator.

• Able to operate and troubleshoot the machinery, tools and equipment

• Must be capable of obtaining & maintaining Fork Truck certifications/licenses.

Performs walkthroughs and documents business processes through flowcharts, narratives, risk and control matrices, and other appropriate documentation to evaluate process design and control effectiveness.

Executes C-SOX testing and other internal control assessments, including walkthroughs, control testing, documentation of results, identification of control deficiencies, and evaluation of the effectiveness of remediation efforts.

Develops and applies appropriate audit testing methodologies, including sampling techniques, data analysis, and other audit procedures consistent with the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) International Professional Practices Framework (IPPF) and applicable organizational standards.

Designs and implements standardized data extraction and analysis procedures across business applications to improve the efficiency, consistency, and effectiveness of audit and control testing.

Analyzes audit results and control deficiencies to identify root causes, assess business impact, and develop practical, risk-based recommendations that strengthen internal controls and improve business processes.

Monitors management action plans and remediation activities related to identified risks and control deficiencies, evaluates progress, and communicates emerging concerns or overdue actions to appropriate stakeholders.

This Global Specialty Products technology team program engineer position is an integral role in the development and implementation of highly efficient and reliable GSP products with superior performance for GE Appliances, a Haier Company. The position will closely interact with sourced suppliers along with the GE Appliances technology, sourcing, quality, and commercial teams to understand all consumer queues in an effort to design and produce new and innovative products that lead the market. The use of skilled engineering analysis and judgment with a strong desire to exceed customer expectations in every way is paramount to position success.

Position
Principal Design Engineer

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

GSP Principal Platform/Design Engineer – RAC, Ventilation Hood, and Garbage Disposer

• Own the definition, development, and maintenance of Product Technical Specifications (PTS) for GSP retail AC, ventilation hood, and garbage disposer platforms, ensuring alignment on performance, reliability, regulatory, safety, and validation requirements

• Lead evaluation and integration of new technologies, including motors, filtration, grinding systems, and connected/digital features

• Own technical leadership as the subject matter expert for ventilation hood and disposer platforms, supporting NPIs, validation strategies, and reliability improvements

• Maintain engineering documentation, CAD models, and technical specifications to ensure platform integrity and reuse

• Support troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement based on field and production feedback

• Support strategic planning activities including project scoping, competitive benchmarking, and contribution to long-term planning (LTP) and investment prioritization

Required Qualifications

• BS degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering or equivalent

• Self-starting leader with 8+ years of engineering experience

• Excellent verbal & written communication and interpersonal skills.

• Proactive problem solver comfortable with hands on work in a laboratory setting to demonstrate solutions

• Demonstrated ability to work in a global environment.

• Demonstrated ability to work multiple design options in parallel.

• Strong project leadership experience and analytical/problem solving skills with demonstrated ability to scope and analyze cross-functional problems to generate/implement solutions.

The Advanced Quality Engineer (AQE) leads quality initiatives for new parts, new processes, and New Product Introductions (NPI) across U.S.-based refrigeration manufacturing sites. This role is responsible for ensuring new equipment, processes, and product changes are launched successfully and transitioned to the plant with sustainable, long-term ownership.
The AQE serves as a key technical resource, applying strong engineering, manufacturing quality, and refrigeration assembly knowledge to solve complex problems independently. This position requires a highly data-driven individual who uses analytical insights to make sound decisions, drive process capability, and improve overall manufacturing quality.
This role primarily supports plant operations in LaFayette, GA.

Position
Advanced Quality Engineer- Cooking

Location
USA, LaFayette, GA

How You'll Create Possibilities

New Product Introductions:

• Own and lead all new equipment qualification activities within the assigned area of responsibility.

• Serve as the process quality expert for assigned equipment, parts, and manufacturing processes.

• Travel to supplier and manufacturing sites for planning meetings, equipment runoffs, and significant production trials.

• Review equipment qualification results and secure leadership approval prior to equipment shipment from suppliers.

• Develop and execute robust qualification plans for new equipment in partnership with Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) and equipment suppliers.

• Lead gage development for production, including specification, design review, cross-functional communication, and final buyoff.

• Facilitate gage kickoff meetings with cross-functional stakeholders, including AME, plant quality engineers, and design engineers.

• Use CMM, 3D scanning, hand gages, and other metrology tools to measure, analyze, and validate parts.

• Lead dimensional analysis reviews for new equipment and build alignment with design engineering and leadership on corrective actions and next steps.

• Partner with cross-functional teams to implement new parts, products, and processes that are sustainable and fully supported after launch.

• Act as a liaison between product design and manufacturing to ensure issues are addressed early and launches occur with minimal disruption.

• Drive Cost of Quality (COQ) improvements, including scrap reduction, yield improvement, concessions, damage reduction, and service call prevention.

• Provide technical leadership in the investigation, development, procurement, and implementation of manufacturing equipment and processes.

• Lead cross-functional PFMEA activities to identify risks associated with new parts and process changes and ensure mitigation actions are implemented before launch.

• Partner with team leaders to develop job instructions, define critical process requirements, and establish standard work and Manufacturing Control Instructions (MCIs).

• Execute drive, strip, and torque studies on new joints to validate torque capability and process robustness.

• Own Quality Management System (QMS) documentation for implemented changes, including Manufacturing Control Plans (MCPs), forms, and MCIs, ensuring compliance with applicable ISO standards.

• Qualify in-house equipment with minimal direction and ensure readiness for production use.

• Interpret technical drawings, including MBD, GD&T, and linear dimensions, and ensure quality plans align with drawing requirements.

• Perform part scanning, CMM analysis, and caliper measurements as needed; additional CMM technician support may be available for broader measurement collection.

What You'll Bring to Our Team

• Bachelor’s Degree or higher in Engineering or another related field

• 2+ years of experience in quality engineering or similar capacity, preferably in the appliance industry.

• Leadership and effective communication experience in the definition, design, implementation and troubleshooting of manufacturing processes.

• Self-starter and influencer – metric driven and willing to work with cross-functional teams and hourly workforce.

• Excellent project tracking and detailed planning skills required.

• Skilled in Microsoft Office applications: Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook.

• Good communicator – data driven, makes decisions based on the data.

• Experience interpreting data to solve manufacturing problems.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Demonstrated leadership and effective communication skills in the definition, design, implementation, and troubleshooting of manufacturing processes

• Experience using, programming, and interpreting CMM, 3D scanning, and other metrology systems

• Strong background in Lean process improvement within high-volume manufacturing environments

• Six Sigma Green Belt or higher certification; proficiency with Minitab preferred

• Experience with metrology and measurement systems, including PolyWorks

• Knowledge of vision systems including Cognex or Keyence camera programming

Working Conditions:

• Up to 10% of domestic and international travel may be required to support supplier equipment runoffs

• Work is performed in a high-volume manufacturing environment

• Personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses and hearing protection, is required

• Frequent walking throughout the manufacturing plant is required

This role combines advanced enterprise data architecture discipline with deep expertise in Artificial Intelligence infrastructure and Data Science enablement to plan, design, deploy, and execute technology solutions aligned to the organization's strategic roadmap.

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

AI Data Layer Enhancement & Transformation (40%)

•
Lead the architectural enhancement and evolution of the enterprise data layer, applying AI-first design principles to unify data across the enterprise value chain (R&D, supply chain, operations, and customer experience).

•
Define, publish, and maintain the Enterprise AI Data Architecture Blueprint—the authoritative reference governing how data flows from source systems (e.g. ERP, CRM, PLM, IoT platforms) through transformation layers to AI models and business outcomes.

•
Design and operationalize an Enterprise AI Data Readiness Framework that continuously assesses, scores, and improves data assets across five core dimensions: Completeness, Consistency, Timeliness, Representativeness, and Fairness.

•
Architect and deploy enterprise-grade vector database infrastructure and build enterprise embedding pipelines that transform structured records, enterprise documents, product manuals, and operational logs into high-quality vector representations.

•
Define the complete data architecture for Large Language Model (LLM) integration, including Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture to support enterprise copilots, customer service, and operational workflows.

•
Design ultra-low latency data serving architectures and event-driven AI data pipelines that feed live AI models in production (e.g., real-time operational analytics, predictive maintenance, and customer insights).

•
Establish an enterprise Synthetic Data Generation capability to augment scarce datasets, generate privacy-safe alternatives to sensitive data, and simulate operational edge cases.

Enterprise Architecture Strategy & Governance (35%)

•
Serve as a strategic partner and governance leader within the EA team, applying and evolving enterprise architecture frameworks (TOGAF, Zachman) with AI-era extensions tailored for a large-scale, complex enterprise environment.

•
Architect modern cloud data warehouse and Lakehouse solutions (e.g. BigQuery) as the unified, ACID-compliant foundation for both analytical and AI/ML workloads on a single governed storage layer.

•
Define and enforce data contracts between data producers (e.g., business operations, product engineering) and AI consumers across all domains to ensure schema, quality, freshness, and semantic consistency.

•
Lead Master Data Management (MDM) strategy with AI entity resolution, enrichment, and disambiguation capabilities embedded in the MDM layer (covering Product, Material, Supplier, and Customer domains).

•
Govern metadata management, data cataloging, and data lineage (e.g. Collibra) and design semantic/context data layers/Knowledge Graph infrastructure to map complex relationships between enterprise assets, suppliers, and business processes.

•
Facilitate Architecture Review Board (ARB) processes for data and AI initiatives, ensuring alignment between project delivery and architectural intent.

•
Align all data architecture decisions with regulatory and compliance requirements without compromising AI agility.

Data Science Enablement & Stakeholder Engagement (15%)

•
Apply statistical expertise to validate data representativeness, distributions, class balance, and sampling strategies for AI training datasets (e.g., ensuring datasets accurately represent real-world operational realities).

•
Serve as a trusted advisor and primary point of contact for business and IT stakeholders on AI data-governed initiatives.

•
Build and maintain effective working relationships at all levels of DT Staff, Extended DT Staff, and business leadership.

•
Proactively identify risks, issues, dependencies, and bottlenecks; implement mitigation strategies to keep teams moving forward.

•
Partner with functional/business teams, DT teams, and other team members to solve problems collaboratively and deliver project objectives.

Data Engineering Oversight & Standards (10%)

•
Provide architectural oversight and define enterprise standards for AI/ML-optimized data pipelines, guiding data engineering delivery teams from raw ingestion through feature engineering.

•
Define the architecture and integration patterns for the Enterprise Feature Store as the central hub of reusable, versioned ML features.

•
Establish DataOps and pipeline governance frameworks, guiding delivery teams on best practices for CI/CD, automated data quality testing gates, and infrastructure-as-code.

•
Define architectural patterns for streaming and event-driven technologies to support high-velocity enterprise and IoT telemetry data.

•
Elicit detailed business and architecture requirements, translating them into clear architectural guidelines and actionable work items for data engineering teams.

The Advanced Quality Engineer (AQE) leads quality activities for new parts, new processes, equipment installations, and New Product Introductions (NPI) across U.S.-based refrigeration manufacturing sites. This role is responsible for ensuring new equipment, processes, and product changes are properly qualified, successfully launched, and transitioned to the plant with sustainable long-term ownership.

The AQE serves as a key technical resource for manufacturing quality, applying strong engineering, problem-solving, data analysis, and refrigeration assembly knowledge to address complex quality and process challenges. The ideal candidate is highly analytical and uses data-driven insights to improve process capability, reduce manufacturing variation, and deliver sustainable quality improvements.

This role primarily supports plant operations in LaFayette, GA, with travel to supplier and manufacturing locations as needed.

Location
USA, LaFayette, GA

New Product Introduction & Launch

• Lead quality activities for new products, parts, processes, and equipment from development through production launch.

• Partner with Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME), Design Engineering, Plant Quality, suppliers, and manufacturing teams to ensure successful and sustainable launches.

• Lead cross-functional PFMEA activities to identify process risks and ensure appropriate mitigation actions are implemented prior to launch.

• Develop and execute qualification plans for new equipment and manufacturing processes in partnership with AME and equipment suppliers.

• Review equipment qualification results and provide technical recommendations and approval for equipment readiness prior to shipment and installation.

• Travel to supplier and manufacturing sites for planning meetings, equipment runoffs, production trials, and launch support.

• Act as a liaison between Product Design and Manufacturing to identify and resolve quality concerns early in the development process.

• Ensure new processes and products are fully transitioned to plant ownership with appropriate documentation, controls, and standard work in place.

Equipment & Process Qualification

• Own and lead equipment and process qualification activities within the assigned area of responsibility.

• Lead dimensional and process capability studies to validate equipment and process performance.

GE Appliances is seeking a Senior Security Engineer, Security Operations to serve as the senior technical lead for the company’s detection and response capability. Day-to-day 24x7 monitoring, alert triage, and vulnerability operations are delivered by our managed security services provider (MSSP); this role is not a shift lead or people manager. Instead, it owns the engineering behind the SOC — the detection and response platforms, detection content, automation, and telemetry — and drives the execution and continuous enhancement of how threats are detected, investigated, and contained across enterprise IT, cloud, and manufacturing (OT) environments. The engineer acts as the MSSP’s technical counterpart and the escalation point for complex incidents, and is accountable for measurable improvements in detection coverage, detection fidelity, and response speed.

Position
Senior Security Engineer- Security Operations

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

How You'll Create Possibilities

Key Responsibilities:

• Serve as the senior technical lead and subject-matter expert for security operations, owning the architecture, configuration, and operational health of the detection and response platforms and setting the technical standards the MSSP operates against.

• Design, build, test, and maintain detection content — correlation rules, behavioral analytics, and IOC/BIOC rules — mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, and manage the full detection lifecycle using detection-as-code practices (version control, testing, peer review, and documentation).

• Own telemetry coverage: identify visibility gaps and onboard, parse, and normalize log sources across endpoints, identity, Microsoft 365, cloud, network, email, DLP, and OT; monitor ingestion health and manage data volume and retention cost.

• Engineer security automation and orchestration (SOAR) playbooks and integrations that enrich alerts, automate containment, and connect security tooling with IT service management and collaboration platforms to reduce manual effort and MSSP handling time.

• Provide technical oversight of MSSP output, in partnership with the Information Security leader who owns the MSSP commercial relationship: review triage and investigation quality, escalation accuracy, and run-book adherence; drive false-positive reduction and tuning; and update MSSP run books and playbooks as detections and the environment change.

• Serve as the Tier 3 escalation point and technical lead for complex or high-severity incidents escalated by the MSSP, performing hands-on investigation, endpoint and log analysis, scoping, and containment, and coordinating with the external incident response retainer when engaged.

• Lead hypothesis-driven threat hunting informed by threat intelligence and threats targeting manufacturing, converting hunt findings into durable detections and hardening recommendations.

• Operationalize threat intelligence by translating advisories, vulnerability disclosures, and adversary reporting into detections, hunts, and blocking actions, and track threat actors relevant to GE Appliances.

• Validate detection and response effectiveness through purple-team exercises, adversary emulation, and breach-and-attack simulation, measuring coverage against MITRE ATT&CK and confirming that the MSSP detects and responds as expected.

• Maintain EDR/XDR platform health across the endpoint and server estate, including agent coverage, prevention and exploit-protection policies, exclusions governance, and response actions.

• Strengthen the technical side of vulnerability operations run by the MSSP, including scan coverage and authenticated scanning, risk-based prioritization using exploitability and threat intelligence (e.g., CISA KEV, EPSS), correlation of vulnerabilities with active threat activity, and automation of remediation workflows.

• Partner with the Cloud, Network, and Identity security engineers to integrate cloud security posture (CNAPP), network, and identity signals into detection and response, including identity threat detection for account takeover, MFA fatigue, and adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) phishing.

• Partner with OT Security to extend monitoring and detection into manufacturing environments in a way that is safe for production and consistent with ISA/IEC 62443 and NIST SP 800-82.

• Author and maintain incident response playbooks, technical run books, and tabletop exercise scenarios, and lead the technical portion of post-incident reviews to drive corrective actions to closure.

• Define, automate, and report operational metrics and KPIs, such as MTTD, MTTR, ATT&CK detection coverage, false-positive rate, log source health, and MSSP escalation quality, to the CISO and Information Security leadership.

• Contribute to the security operations roadmap; evaluate emerging capabilities, including AI-assisted triage and investigation and agentic SOC automation; and support platform evaluations, proofs of concept, and total cost of ownership (TCO) analyses.

• Provide technical evidence for logging, monitoring, and incident response controls in SOX, C-SOX, PCI-DSS, and other audits, and drive remediation of related findings.

• Mentor engineers and transfer knowledge to MSSP analysts on the GE Appliances environment, detections, and response procedures.

What You'll Bring to Our Team

Requirements & Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 6–10 years of progressive experience in IT or information security, with at least 4+ years of hands-on experience in security operations, detection engineering, or incident response in a large enterprise environment.

• Deep hands-on experience engineering and administering SIEM/SOAR and EDR/XDR platforms (e.g., Palo Alto Networks Cortex XSIAM/XDR, Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel/Defender, CrowdStrike), including writing detection rules and queries (e.g., XQL, SPL, KQL).

• Proven experience building detection content mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and tuning it for fidelity at enterprise scale.

• Experience building SOAR playbooks and integrations, with proficiency in Python and/or PowerShell and working with REST APIs and JSON.

• Hands-on incident response experience with significant enterprise incidents such as ransomware, business email compromise (BEC), and account takeover, including endpoint, log, and network analysis.

• Experience working with an MSSP or MDR provider in a technical oversight role, including tuning, escalation quality review, and run-book development.

• Strong understanding of log sources and telemetry across Windows, Linux, network, cloud (AWS, Azure, and/or GCP), Microsoft 365, and identity providers.

• Working knowledge of frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, NIST SP 800-61 (incident handling), NIST CSF, and CIS Controls.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate with both technical and executive audiences.

We are seeking an experienced Electrical Engineer to lead and support plant electrical infrastructure, capital equipment, and facility-related projects across a large manufacturing campus. This role is responsible for managing electrical distribution systems, supporting equipment installations and retooling activities, coordinating contractors and vendors, and ensuring projects are executed safely, on schedule, and within budget. The Electrical Engineer will work closely with maintenance, operations, AME teams, skilled trades, and external contractors to support business needs and maintain safe, reliable, and compliant plant electrical systems.

Position
Electrical Engineer

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

How You'll Create Possibilities

Key Responsibilities

• Create, update, and maintain single-line drawings for plant-level electrical distribution systems.

• Oversee power distribution and coordination across the site.

• Evaluate and update breaker settings, coordination studies, short circuit studies, voltage drop calculations, and arc flash models to support ongoing manufacturing changes.

• Coordinate specifications, vendor selection, purchase, and installation of high-voltage electrical distribution gear.

• Provide technical expertise on electrical infrastructure constraints, utility bottlenecks, and corrective actions.

Equipment Installation and Retooling Support

• Coordinate electrical disconnects, cleanup, and removal of existing equipment being dispositioned for retooling.

• Work with equipment AMEs to define power requirements, feeder locations, and installation needs, and document accordingly.

• Support equipment installation, commissioning, qualification, and startup activities.

Design, Review, and Field Support

• Perform detailed design for large projects, including:

• Drawing mark-ups

• Load calculations

• Coordination studies

• Short circuit calculations

• Voltage drop calculations

• Equipment specifications

• Compliance with applicable codes and company standards

• Conduct design reviews for large projects to ensure system compatibility, conformance, and constructability.

• Provide field inspection and implementation support for:

• Electrical systems

• Security systems

• Fire alarm systems

• Data/telecom systems

• Instrumentation and controls

• Review electrical power, instrumentation, and control drawings.

• Review and approve changes to electrical drawings and related documentation.

• Review and approve change records that have electrical impacts to validated systems.

Safety, Compliance, and Contractor Coordination

• Support and drive an efficient subcontracting process in collaboration with the maintenance group.

• Oversee outsourced work to ensure contractor performance, quality, and compliance.

• Drive a safe and environmentally compliant project environment, especially for high-risk work such as:

• High-voltage work

• Working at heights

• Demolition

• Abatement

• Maintain compliance with training, safe work plans, Avetta utilization, and company safety processes.

• Ensure all equipment and installations comply with applicable industry and governmental EHS standards.

• Apply Human Organizational Performance (HOP) principles to prioritize health and safety in all projects and process changes.

Operational and Team Support

• Provide technical support to maintenance and operations teams on electrical-related issues.

• Support teams on plant projects and day-to-day business needs.

• Identify, scope, and manage energy conservation projects.

• Work effectively across cross-functional teams, including salaried employees, shop floor operators, skilled trades, suppliers, and contractors.

What You'll Bring to Our Team

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related engineering discipline, or equivalent hands-on technical/manufacturing experience.

• 7+ years of experience in procurement, testing, installation, and support of manufacturing equipment, infrastructure, and process improvement.

• Experience managing capital equipment procurement projects, including specification development, supplier selection, technical reviews, and installation/qualification.

• Previous experience in a large-scale manufacturing environment.

• Strong knowledge of industrial electrical systems, standards, codes, and construction practices.

• Ability to read and interpret:

• Single-line drawings

• Ladder logic/control drawings

• Electrical power drawings

• Instrumentation and control drawings

• Strong understanding of engineering principles and electrical system design techniques.

• Knowledge of the full project lifecycle, including initiation, design, construction, and commissioning/validation.

• Strong organizational, project management, and communication skills.

• Ability to work effectively in both team-based and self-managed environments with minimal supervision.

Preferred Qualifications

• EIT or PE registration preferred.

• Familiarity with Lean manufacturing principles.

• Experience with high-voltage electrical distribution equipment and plant infrastructure systems.

• Experience supporting validated systems and change management processes.

• Experience coordinating contractors, subcontractors, and plant maintenance resources.

• Prior leadership or people-management experience is preferred but not required.
